key_facts: patient is a man in his 40s
patient has stage IV KRAS wild-type rectal adenocarcinoma
patient has pulmonary and liver metastases
patient has undergone radiation therapy and multiple chemotherapy cycles
lesion is not associated with pain or pruritus
genetic analysis was performed using paired whole-exome sequencing

raw.rationale: The presence of a rapidly growing, well-defined vascular lesion with discrete clusters of small-caliber vessels and a somatic KDR (VEGFR2) mutation supports the diagnosis of Angiosarcoma, which is a rare and aggressive malignancy of endothelial origin.

rejected.label: Tufted Angioma
rejected.why: Typically presents in childhood and has a distinct cannonball pattern on histology, which is not described in this case.

rejected.label: Pyogenic Granuloma
rejected.why: Usually associated with trauma, infection, or irritation, and has a characteristic histological appearance with a collarette of epithelial cells, which is not present in this case.

rejected.label: Telangiectasia Macularis Eruptiva Perstans
rejected.why: A rare condition characterized by multiple telangiectasias, but the presence of a single, large lesion and the KDR mutation makes this diagnosis less likely.

rejected.label: Kaposi's Sarcoma
rejected.why: Typically associated with human herpesvirus 8 infection and has a distinct histological appearance with spindle cell proliferation, which is not described in this case.
